declared_deviations.what: no separate terminal Adj event is emitted
declared_deviations.why: spec §3 recomputes after every registration and the vendored P0 Harness does exactly that inside each registration event, but it exposes no public Adj emitter; the import writes through the registration API only and never forges a log line, so the terminal adjudication is the state after the last event

declared_deviations.what: imported FCL problem records use SpawnTrigger.SEED
declared_deviations.why: the vendored enum has no 'import' member; 'seed' is the only trigger that does not assert an in-graph derivation. The clean fix is an enum addition, requested rather than papered over

declared_deviations.what: research problems use SpawnTrigger.RESEARCH with empty criteria
declared_deviations.why: the vendored enum has the member and §12 is exactly this path, but the trigger is not part of the v1.3 enum text; criteria stay empty because no instantiated commitment id is a criterion

declared_deviations.what: document-local depends refs are dropped, not turned into dep edges
declared_deviations.why: at node granularity they would be dep self-loops, i.e. cycles; toposort rejects them and a self-loop asserts nothing the author declared

declared_deviations.what: a self-targeting objection mints no warrant
declared_deviations.why: a Dung self-attack means 'this argument is self-defeating', which is not what an intra-document caveat asserts; minting it would flip two labels for reasons that have nothing to do with the evidence

declared_deviations.what: an objection against a record this import reified as a warrant attacks that warrant's validity node, not the node artifact
declared_deviations.why: spec §1 closure: attackers of a validity node attack the warrant and every carrier of it, so criticism of a criticism keeps its force instead of collapsing into a plain edge onto the carrier

declared_deviations.what: the retargeting rule above has ONE exception: an objection against a criticism carried by the SAME artifact is not retargeted
declared_deviations.why: the §1 closure lifts an attack on a validity node onto every carrier of the warrant, and for an intra-document criticism of a criticism that carrier is the objector itself, so retargeting would mint a self-attack through the closure and make the artifact self-defeating - which is not what an author asserts by qualifying their own earlier objection. `objection.o4` against `o1`/`o2` is exactly this case; it is dropped, not retargeted, and counted under its own code so the loss is visible rather than silent

declared_deviations.what: an FCL `claim` record maps to no spec construct
declared_deviations.why: a claim asserts content without proposing a test, so it is neither an observation-valued commitment nor a criticism nor a problem; it survives in the artifact body and in the FCL-1 document artifact, and is reported here because `uptake_refs_unmapped` covers only the claims the author put in `uptake`

invariant_i7: **No label produced by this import is a semantic attribution.** Statuses are mechanism bookkeeping over the imported attack relation; they do not bear on the FCL-1 hypothesis, on FW5, or on the merit of any contribution. Root alone interprets substantive output (PROTOCOL.md §Interpretation).
multi_arm_framing: This scope contains 3 arms (bare, mini_prose, native) whose declared commitment surface is prose and 1 arm (mini_fcl) whose surface is FCL-1. A prose commitment surface is never parsed, so no warrant, no attack edge and no refuted label can arise from a prose arm under this import. The distribution of statuses across arms is therefore a property of the carrier this importer reads, not a comparison between the arms. Any cross-arm reading is root's, not this instrument's.

problems.description: I share a flat with two friends. We keep arguing about ordinary household chores. Sometimes we agree on who will do something, but later we disagree about what the agreement meant. Our work schedules change, and one friend has started avoiding the conversations. What should I do?

Whether shortening or restructuring the check-in will make the withdrawing friend more willing to participate is unknown, and if the withdrawal is about something other than chores, no scheduling change will reach it.
Whether the account's own c6 was meant to bound the proposal or only to annotate it is not determinable from the text; the answer changes whether my objection o2 lands.

I do not have evidence about this specific flat's actual distribution of work; my objection rests on the account not excluding the imbalance reading, not on a claim that the imbalance reading is true here.

How can a flat distinguish underspecification from positional struggle using only what its members can observe? The two produce similar surface evidence: recurring arguments, memory disagreement, one person disengaging.
What should the flat do if the positional reading is correct? The contribution stops short of an answer and should not be read as supplying one.

Whether the withdrawing friend is avoiding the chore conversations specifically or avoiding the flat's company more generally is not distinguishable from the task description, and the two call for different responses.
I have no evidence about this flat's actual distribution of work, and I will not convert the objection's point that the imbalance reading is not excluded into a claim that the imbalance is real here.

Observation-valued commitment with no covering evidence (daily/mini_fcl/cycle01/account#c3): If this account is taken up, the first move is to try naming the scope of each agreement at the moment it is made, distinguishing this-week instances from standing roles.

Observation-valued commitment with no covering evidence (daily/mini_fcl/cycle01/account#c4): Treat schedule change as normal input and give it a scheduled place, rather than treating a swap request as a breach.

Observation-valued commitment with no covering evidence (daily/mini_fcl/cycle01/rival#r4): Try naming what each person does not want to lose before attempting any chore allocation, and treat the result as diagnostic rather than as a settlement.

Observation-valued commitment with no covering evidence (daily/mini_fcl/cycle01/response#m2): Pick one diagnostic and run it before committing to a remedy, choosing by cost rather than by conviction; if the flat has one meeting's worth of patience, use the fortnight tally first.

Observation-valued commitment with no covering evidence (daily/mini_fcl/cycle01/response#m4): Ask the withdrawing person what they are declining, not whether the format is hard, and ask before changing the format, because a gentler channel can be the most effective way to keep a refusal from being heard.

Observation-valued commitment with no covering evidence (daily/mini_fcl/cycle01/carry#r4): Ask the withdrawing friend what they are declining, not only whether the format is hard, and ask before changing the format; a gentler channel can lower the cost of silent non-participation as easily as the cost of participation.
